title: How Do Steel Ships Float? 🚢 #shorts
description:
A steel bar sinks instantly, so how does a ship made of thousands of tons of steel float? Anything in water is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of the water it pushes aside (Archimedes' principle). A solid block of steel displaces only a little water, far less than its own weight, so it sinks. Shape the same steel into a hollow hull and it displaces far more. Most of a ship's inside is air, so its average density ends up lower than water's, and it settles until the water it displaces weighs exactly as much as the ship. That's why ships carry load lines, or Plimsoll marks, showing how deep they can safely sit; in fresh water, which is less dense, they ride lower.
